races.title: State Assembly, District 10
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Stephanie Nguyen
cands.bio: Democrat representing California Assembly District 10 since December 2022. Former executive director of Asian Resources, Inc. in Sacramento and earlier director of the Sacramento Asian Pacific Chamber Foundation. Served on the Elk Grove City Council from 2017 to 2022, including a term as vice mayor in 2020.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Teachers Association, IUOE Local 3, California Young Democrats and Sacramento County Young Democrats.

Her campaign site features endorsements from Assemblymember Jim Cooper, Assemblymember Kevin McCarty, State Treasurer Fiona Ma, former State Senator Deborah Ortiz, Rep. Ami Bera and Elk Grove Mayor Bobbie Singh-Allen.

cands.gaps: Her birthplace city was not found; sources say only that she was born in the United States. The date she came to California was not found, because she appears to have been raised in Sacramento. No statements or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, slowing growth, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun laws, abortion, school choice or teacher pay were found in the pages read. Her policy priorities page and the list of bills she sponsored were not readable in the pages collected. She did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. Her campaign site appears to date from her 2022 run, so its statements may be out of date. No controversies or foreign ties were found in the pages read.

local.label: Roots 90: Ballotpedia says she was raised in Sacramento, and her campaign site says she grew up in Sacramento's Little Saigon, attended Sacramento schools and has lived in Elk Grove for over 18 years; Wikipedia says only that she was born in the US to Vietnamese refugees, with no birthplace city.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Elk Grove City Council member 2017-2022 (appointed, then elected in 2018; vice mayor 2020), Assembly member since December 2022, and about 15 years as executive director of Asian Resources, Inc., a nonprofit her campaign site says has an $8 million budget.
qual.why: She has held legislative office at both the city and state level, and ran an organization with a sizable budget; the budget figure comes from her campaign site. No law or formal policy career appears in the pages read.
qual.label: She has held legislative office at both the city and state level, and ran an organization with a sizable budget; the budget figure comes from her campaign site. No law or formal policy career appears in the pages read.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says public safety is a priority, that she will be 'a fierce advocate for keeping us safe' in the Assembly, and that she has the support of local peace officers; it names no specific bill or penalty. This is a campaign statement from her earlier run.

cands.name: Vinaya Singh
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 10 in 2024 and 2026. Holds a PhD in Management. Says he worked as a scientist for the Indian Space Research Organization and later for IT companies in the U.S. Has not held public office.

endorsements.text: 2026: listed on three online voter-guide recommendations: April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide.

cands.gaps: We could not find when Vinaya Singh moved to California or where he has lived since. His birthplace is given only as a remote village in India. He has held no public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, guns, abortion, H-1B visas or teacher pay. His campaign site offers a general pledge to fight special interests but no specific promise to refuse any kind of contribution. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. The 'About' page on his campaign site was cut off after the first paragraph, so the rest of his life story was not read. Parts of his campaign site still refer to the 2024 election.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Computer engineering degrees (BS and MS), then work with the Indian Space Research Organization and with IT companies in the U.S., plus a PhD in Management, according to his campaign site. No elected office, legislative, policy or budget work is documented.
qual.why: He has a long career in science and IT that is unrelated to writing law and budgets, and he has no legislative or local elected experience. This puts him in the low band for the office.
qual.label: He has a long career in science and IT that is unrelated to writing law and budgets, and he has no legislative or local elected experience. This puts him in the low band for the office.

workers-first.evidence: He says he opposes open borders and sanctuary policies and calls for repealing California's Sanctuary State status and prioritizing services for citizens over asylum seekers.

back-police-order.evidence: He says AB 109 and Props. 47 and 57 must be repealed, that district attorneys should be required to prosecute criminals, and that law enforcement should be allowed to do their jobs.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: He proposes giving builders of low-cost housing the same relief from environmental regulations and fees that sports stadium builders receive.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: He says parents should have the right to move their child to another public or charter school and that local school boards should control curriculum. He does not mention vouchers or teacher pay.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Proposes providing 'the same relief from environmental regulations and fees that builders of sports stadiums and other local revenue boosters receive, so that low-cost homes can be available for the poor and the homeless.'
